books.section: Topic 8.13 The environment and natural resources from 1968 to 1980
The New Left, Feminism, and the Counterculture

source: original; stimulus photograph viewed before writing

stimulus.source_note: Photograph: protesters at the Earth Day flag ceremony, Washington Monument, Washington, D.C., April 22, 1970, public domain (U.S. National Park Service photograph, via Wikimedia Commons; file dated April 22, 1970). Participation figure verified against the EPA's Earth Day history and EarthDay.org: about 20 million Americans. Account drawn from the grounding books (Barron's Ch. 10, Topic 8.13, 'The Environmental Movement').
stimulus.text:
The photograph shows the first Earth Day, April 22, 1970, at the Washington Monument in Washington, D.C. Seen from above, a large crowd gathers around an American flag on a paved plaza. One protester holds a sign reading 'END THE RAPE OF AMERICA,' and several photographers film the crowd.

Senator Gaylord Nelson of Wisconsin proposed the event as a nationwide teach-in, modeled on the teach-ins of the antiwar movement. About 20 million Americans took part in rallies, cleanups, and campus events across the country.

stem: The teach-in model for Earth Day best shows which of the following about the environmental movement?

options.text: It copied its tactics from the oil industry.
options.misconception: Background: The oil industry was the target of the movement, not its model for organizing.

options.text: It refused to learn from any earlier movement.
options.misconception: The passage says Earth Day was modeled on the teach-ins of the antiwar movement.

options.text: It was organized entirely by the federal government.
options.misconception: Background: Earth Day was organized by Senator Nelson and a staff of young activists, not by the federal government.

options.text: It borrowed organizing methods from the antiwar movement.

rationales.A: Background: The oil industry was the target of the movement, not its model for organizing.
rationales.B: The passage says Earth Day was modeled on the teach-ins of the antiwar movement.
rationales.C: Background: Earth Day was organized by Senator Nelson and a staff of young activists, not by the federal government.
rationales.D: The passage says Nelson proposed a nationwide teach-in modeled on the teach-ins of the antiwar movement.
rationales.general:
1. The passage names the model directly: a nationwide teach-in.
2. Background: Teach-ins were the antiwar movement's way of teaching a campus about a cause, and Earth Day copied that form.
3. Background: Many early environmental activists were veterans of the antiwar movement, so the borrowing was personal as well as tactical.
Remember: A movement's tactics often come from the movements its people came from.
